extracted_claims.text: Article 113 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the original AI Act) sets the general date of application as 2 August 2026.

Under the original AI Act, obligations for high-risk AI systems laid down in Sections 1, 2 and 3 of Chapter III (which includes the Annex III high-risk classification and requirements) were due to apply from 2 August 2026.

The Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) amends the AI Act to postpone the application of Chapter III, Sections 1-3 for Annex III high-risk AI systems from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027.
The Digital Omnibus on AI also postpones obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I from (originally) 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) was published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026 and entered into force on 27 July 2026, days before the original 2 August 2026 deadline.
The AI Omnibus (Digital Omnibus on AI) was proposed by the European Commission on 19 November 2025.

As of the Digital Omnibus, the Commission's original proposal envisioned that Chapter III high-risk obligations would only apply once the Commission adopted a Decision confirming completion of standards/guidance, with a 6-month transition for Annex III and 12-month transition for Annex I after that, with backstop application dates of 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) if no such Decision were made.
The deferral of Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 is described as a 16-month postponement from the original 2 August 2026 date.
The AI Act Amendment (Digital Omnibus) extends compliance deadlines for high-risk AI systems by 18 months for some systems and two years for others relative to the original 2 August 2026 deadline.
The 2 August 2026 deadline for transparency requirements under Article 50 (for certain AI systems) remains in place and is not affected by the high-risk deadline postponement.
As of a provisional political agreement reported on 6 May 2026, the postponement of Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 was pending formal adoption rather than final law.

Some commentary (as of an article corrected 3 October 2026) initially and incorrectly stated that AI Act high-risk obligations would become enforceable on 2 August 2026 and described the Digital Omnibus as an uncertain proposal from February 2026, before correcting that the Omnibus was proposed 19 November 2025 and in force since 27 July 2026.
Some sources describe the Annex III high-risk deadline moving to 2027 as a 'confirmed, binding change' under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

The exact date of formal adoption of the Digital Omnibus on AI is unclear given one source describes a provisional political agreement around 6 May 2026 while others describe the regulation as already published in the Official Journal (24 July 2026) and in force (27 July 2026) — the precise legislative timeline and vote history is not fully reconciled across sources.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Chapter III, Sections 1–3, including Annex III classification requirements (high confidence). A Digital Omnibus on AI, cited as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, reportedly postpones this deadline for Annex III systems to 2 December 2027 and delays obligations for Annex I-embedded high-risk systems to 2 August 2028, but this postponement rests on only medium-confidence corroboration (0.56), and at least one source describes it as still a "provisional political agreement" pending formal adoption as of May 2026 rather than confirmed law. Readers should treat the exact legislative status and final adoption timeline of the postponement as unresolved rather than settled fact.

## Key Findings

### Original Statutory Deadline
Article 113 of the original AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes 2 August 2026 as the general date of application for the Regulation ([EUR-Lex IMMC document](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836), [OJ L_202601744](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=OJ%3AL_202601744)) (high confidence). Obligations in Chapter III, Sections 1–3 — covering classification of Annex III systems as high-risk and associated compliance requirements — were originally due to apply from this same date ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-113), [Akin Gump](https://www.akingump.com/en/insights/alerts/EU-AI-act-amendments-defer-and-clarify-obligations), [William Fry](https://www.williamfry.com/knowledge/is-your-annex-iii-ai-system-high-risk-definitely-maybe)) (high confidence).

### Reported Postponement via the Digital Omnibus on AI
Multiple sources report that a Digital Omnibus on AI, identified as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, amends the AI Act to defer application of Chapter III, Sections 1–3 for Annex III high-risk systems from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2), [Gibson Dunn](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes), [FPF](https://fpf.org/blog/the-ai-act-implementation-timeline-what-changes-under-the-ai-omnibus)) (medium confidence, corroboration score 0.56). This is described as a roughly 16-month postponement from the original date by one source ([The Professor](https://www.theprofessor.info/insights/eu-ai-act-delay-what-moved-and-what-did-not)) (low confidence). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I are reportedly postponed from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028 ([McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026), [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-deadline-omnibus-20260)) (medium confidence). One source instead frames the combined extensions more loosely as "18 months for some systems and two years for others" ([Akin Gump](https://www.akingump.com/en/insights/alerts/EU-AI-act-amendments-defer-and-clarify-obligations)) (low confidence), which does not precisely align with the specific figures reported elsewhere.

### Legislative Timeline — Unsettled
Accounts of the legislative process conflict. One source reports the Commission proposed the Digital Omnibus on 19 November 2025 ([McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)) (low confidence) and that the Regulation was published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026 and entered into force on 27 July 2026, days before the original deadline ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-deadline-omnibus-20260)) (low confidence). By contrast, another source describes only a "provisional political agreement" as of 6 May 2026, with formal adoption still pending ([Alation](https://www.alation.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-guide)) (low confidence). The Commission's original proposal reportedly envisioned linking application to a Commission Decision confirming completion of standards, with transition periods and backstop dates of 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) ([Winston Taylor](https://www.winstontaylor.com/insights/ai-act-rules-on-high-risk-ai-delayed-as-ai-digital-omnibus-agreed)) (low confidence), leaving unclear whether fixed dates or a conditional mechanism ultimately governs.

### Unaffected Obligations
The 2 August 2026 deadline for transparency requirements under Article 50 remains unchanged and is not affected by any high-risk deadline postponement ([AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [Akin Gump](https://www.akingump.com/en/insights/alerts/EU-AI-act-amendments-defer-and-clarify-obligations)) (high confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources ([William Fry](https://www.williamfry.com/knowledge/is-your-annex-iii-ai-system-high-risk-definitely-maybe), [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)) state or imply the 2 August 2026 deadline remained effective, appearing outdated relative to later reports of a postponement. There is direct tension between sources treating the Omnibus as already enacted law in force since July 2026 ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-deadline-omnibus-20260), low confidence) and a source describing it as still a provisional political agreement as of May 2026 ([Alation](https://www.alation.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-guide), low confidence) — this discrepancy is central and unresolved. Characterizations of extension lengths also vary (16 months vs. "18 months/two years"), suggesting imprecision or differing groupings of affected systems across sources (both low confidence). One source frames the 2027 postponement as a "confirmed, binding change" ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)), though this is a low-confidence claim given limited corroboration and conflicts with the provisional-agreement framing above.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the Commission's proposed mechanism tying application dates to a Decision confirming standards completion was retained in the final text, or whether 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 are fixed, unconditional dates. The precise legislative history — proposal, political agreement, and formal adoption dates — is not reconciled across sources, and no single high-authority source confirms the Omnibus's final enacted status with certainty. It is also unclear whether Annex III sub-categories face differentiated timelines.
